name: La Paz (Baja)
coordsNote: Malecón / Centro, La Paz, Baja California Sur (the walkable waterfront where most long-stay visitors base themselves).

english.note: Good in town (expat hub — above national average)
english.rationale: Mexico sits in EF EPI's low band (score 440), which maps to tier 1 country-wide; Baja California Sur scores 483 on the same index, well above the national figure, and La Paz has a long-established North American snowbird/expat community around the Malecón, so it gets the +1 expat-hub bump (as Mérida and San Miguel de Allende do).

sources.title: EF EPI — Mexico
sources.note: Regional table on the same page lists Baja California Sur at 483.

vibe: Calm bay-front state capital; islands, whale sharks and winter sun
narrative: A working Mexican state capital strung along a long seafront malecón, with Balandra's shallow turquoise lagoon and the sea-lion colonies of Espíritu Santo island a short boat ride away and juvenile whale sharks in the bay through the winter. Summers are fiercely hot and August–October brings hurricane risk; nomad infrastructure is thinner than in Mexico's big hubs.

season.rationale: Snowbirds return from mid-October as heat and hurricane risk ease and leave before May; December–March is the busiest stretch (whale-shark peak, holidays, Carnaval). June–September is very quiet: brutal heat and hurricane risk, with many locals and expats leaving the peninsula.

sources.title: Gringo Gazette — snowbird season in Baja Sur
sources.quote: starting in the middle of October, as the heat trails off and the chance of a hurricane decreases, those here year-round start to welcome those returning

sources.title: Mexico Travel & Leisure — best time to visit La Paz

safety.propertyNote: Calm malecón and Centro; modest petty theft
safety.womensSafetyNote: Perceived insecurity well below the national average; women's perception nationally higher
safety.touristRationale: State violence is largely intra-criminal and concentrated outside the waterfront and tourist areas; La Paz residents report markedly less insecurity than the national average.

homicideOverride.source: INEGI 2024 death-registration homicides, Baja California Sur (85; rate 10/100k vs national 25.6), via Expansión Política

rationale.property: Editorial estimate: no city property-crime series found; INEGI's ENSU urban survey puts La Paz's perceived insecurity at 46.6% vs 61.5% nationally (Mar 2026), and the walkable Centro/malecón is low-key. Set level with Oaxaca (70), below Mérida (80), well above Mexico City (45).
rationale.tourist: 1.08 like Mexico City: a moderate tourist-zones-safer adjustment. State homicide (10/100k INEGI 2024, double 2023's ~5) reflects drug-market disputes mostly away from the waterfront; Mérida/Oaxaca get 1.12 but their violence is either very low or clearly regional.
rationale.womens: +10 on the country Gallup baseline (Oaxaca +11, Mérida +25): La Paz's ENSU insecurity perception is ~15 points under the national figure; INEGI notes women nationally feel less safe than men, so the uplift is kept moderate.

selection: Sea of Cortez winter-sun base for North American snowbirds in a Level-2 state (Baja California Sur): Nov–Apr season, whale sharks and islands, with a clear Aug–Oct hurricane window to plan around.
researchNotes: Advisory: travel.state.gov returned a Cloudflare bot check (not bypassed); level/text/state entry and date come from the State Dept's official feeds (cadataapi.state.gov TravelAdvisories: published 2025-08-11T20:00-04:00; RSS pubDate Tue 12 Aug 2025). The catalog's other Mexican cities carry 2026-05-29 — reconcile centrally if the page shows a later reissue date. Baja California Sur: Level 2 with no U.S.-government travel restrictions. Homicide override is STATE scope (La Paz municipality figure not found in a citable source; Los Cabos accounts for much of the state's violence, so La Paz may be lower). Timezone: Zona Pacífico (UTC-7), no DST since the Oct 2022 time-zone law (only Baja California and northern border municipalities still change). Hazards: summer heat (Jul–Sep highs ~35 °C) left to the climate pipeline; only one hazard per month, so hurricanes take Aug–Oct. Whale-shark end month (May) is from a travel guide; the SEMARNAT plan says animals leave Jun–Jul but the regulated tour window can be shorter. Gray-whale lagoon trips (Magdalena Bay, Jan–Mar) are a day trip, not listed as a city event. Review edit 2026-10-03: September hurricane flag lowered from level 2 to 1 to match Mérida's Aug-Oct treatment (level 2 is kept for extreme heat/peak typhoon exposure).
